transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Hello, this is calling from our company. Is this a good time to talk about your account?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.message: What the hell do you think? No, it's not a good time—and it's never a good damn time! You people call me every day like I don't have enough on my plate after losing my job!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message:
I’m really sorry you’re going through this, and I appreciate you being honest with me—I can hear how stressed this situation is making you. You’re absolutely right; losing your job is an incredibly difficult thing, and I’m not here to add to your burden. My name is Sarah, and I’m with Acme Financial. I’m not calling to pressure you. I’m calling because I want to see if we can figure out a way forward that actually works for you right now.

Would you be open to talking—when you’re ready—about what kind of payment, if any, might be manageable given your current situation? We do have options, like pausing payments for a short time or setting up a plan based on what you can afford, even if it's little right now. I’m here to help find a solution, not make things harder.

If now isn’t a good time, I completely understand. We can schedule a better time to talk, or you can let me know how you’d prefer to handle things. I’m listening.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.message: Alright... look, I don’t need some canned sympathy, but—fine. You’re not screaming at me like the last guy. I’m tapped out, Sarah. Zero coming in right now. But I ain’t just gonna ghost on this forever. I *do* want to fix it—when I can. You got anything that doesn’t involve magic money appearing outta nowhere?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message:
Thank you for trusting me with that, and for wanting to do the right thing—that matters, and I see that. You don’t owe me an apology for being honest. Honestly, I appreciate it.

And no magic money needed. What we *can* do is work with reality—your reality. Since you’re not bringing in income right now, the most important thing is to avoid making things harder on yourself. What I *can* offer—right now—is a **payment holiday** for up to 90 days. That means no payments required, and we’ll pause any collection activity. It’s not a permanent fix, but it gives you breathing room while you focus on getting back on your feet.

At the same time, I can help you set up a plan to revisit this in a few weeks—say, once you’ve applied for a few jobs or maybe started receiving unemployment, if you aren’t already. And when the time comes, we can look at a realistic payment plan based on actual income.

Would something like that give you the space you need? I can also send all of this in writing if you’d like—no calls, just information in your inbox—until you’re ready to talk again. You’re not ghosting; you’re regrouping. And that’s totally valid.
